index.purpose: Makes upstream's one-stage HIP custom all-reduce correct on two cards linked over PCIe only. The kernel is a pull design: each rank copies its input into a staging buffer and the peer reads it through an IPC mapping; taken from the PyTorch pool, that buffer showed the peer the previous payload (RAD-2: wrong sums, noise from the first token). When the group is not fully XGMI-linked the HIP constructor allocates the staging buffer with `allocate_meta_buffer` (uncached fine-grained memory, the class of the signal buffer), and `should_custom_ar` declines every input that does not fit it (`max_size − 1` bytes; `SGLANG_RDNA4_CUSTOM_AR_MAX_BYTES` lowers the limit), so prefill chunks stay on RCCL and the in-place IPC path is never taken. Logged once per group (`[RDNA4] custom all-reduce: uncached staging buffer on a PCIe-linked group, inputs above N bytes stay on RCCL`). No change under `--disable-custom-all-reduce` or without `SGLANG_USE_1STAGE_ALLREDUCE=1`; the FP8 `qwen38` preset and the `flint` preset drop the flag and export the switch (`ENABLE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE=0` restores RCCL; flint reads +2.6 % no-spec decode at four depths, FLINT-4b), every other preset stays on RCCL. Two bare ranks (`scripts/bench/allreduce_rows_ladder.py`): exact sums eager and in a 130-reduction graph, 10.8 / 22.3 / 32.2 / 58.9 µs per reduction against RCCL's 17.8 / 29.5 / 38.9 / 61.2 at 1 / 9 / 16 / 32 rows. index.purpose: On HIP the attention-TP sum takes an FP32 detour (cast up, all-reduce, cast down) unless the model's update policy opts out (080).
